text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- In a strongly-worded statement, Land and Co-operative Development Minister Osu Sukam charged on Monday that state governments had "shortchanged" landowners in enforcing the Land Acquisition Act.

-- Shares of North Borneo Timbers Bhd and Construction & Supplies House Bhd continued to be in the limelight at the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on rumours of a possible merger between the two timber-related firms.
-- Expatriates who get approval for work permits from ministries and agencies will be endorsed by the Immigration Department the same day if the documents are in order.

-- Improvements at the workplace, higher wages and attractive labour regulations have contributed to making Malaysia's industrial relations one of the most conducive in the world, according to a report on global competitiveness.

-- Most analysts welcome the suggestion for Malaysian banks to expand their operations overseas but pointed out that efficient service needs to be provided if the companies want to be competitive with their more established foreign counterparts.
